note: Self-contained oracle case (stdlib only, not replay-driven), proven directly with effect='canary_write'. Held out: written after the compact profile and the oracle were frozen, from the public Django advisory CVE-2021-31542 (uploaded file names). No upstream repo/commit applies: the code is an original reimplementation of the vulnerable pattern, not Django.

real_world_analog.fix: Django 3.2.1, 3.1.9 and 2.2.21 apply stricter basename and path sanitation to uploaded file names (django.core.files.utils.validate_file_name rejects names with path elements and the names '', '.' and '..'; the commit is 0b79eb36915d178aef5c6a7bbce71b1e76d376d3). The fixed tree rejects such names with an original check.
real_world_analog.summary: Potential directory traversal via uploaded files: MultiPartParser, UploadedFile and FieldFile allowed directory traversal with suitably crafted file names. Affected Django 2.2 before 2.2.21, 3.1 before 3.1.9 and 3.2 before 3.2.1; severity low by Django's policy.
real_world_analog.verification: CVE number, release notes and fix commit confirmed via web search (Django weblog, release notes, CVE record, GitHub commit) on 2026-10-31; the service in this case is original code written from that description, not Django.

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the name starts with a sub-directory ('sub/../../...'), so a screen that only looks at how the name begins lets it through and it still climbs out of the storage directory; the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
